Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — very helpful. Our procurement team is compiling a set of operational controls we need to include in the DPA annex and the Data Processing Framework (DPF) section of our RFP. Two specific asks came up that we couldn't find explicit answers for in the public docs:

1) When a Clearmont request is routed to a Redwood-hosted model in the US, is any model state or KV cache persisted to disk on the host beyond the lifetime of the request? We need explicit language for our DPA annex about transient cache vs. persisted artifacts.

2) We require clarity on cross-border runtime exports: if a request is proxied through an EU edge then routed to a US GPU instance for inference, what technical safeguards ensure that request payloads and derived intermediate artifacts are not retained or accessible outside of the US region? Please point to logs/audit trails we can reference.

Can you provide a short operational statement and any supporting evidence (screenshots, logs, or a control matrix) we can include in the response? We are on a tight timeline for legal review; target is COB Monday.

Hi Hannah — thanks for the clear asks. Quick summary up front, then I can route formal evidence:

- KV / runtime caches: Redwood’s serving runtime keeps per-request KV cache in-memory only. We do not persist KV caches to local disk by default. Persistent artifacts (model checkpoints, quantized weights) are deployed as read-only model files managed by our deployment service; these are static and not request-derived.

- Cross-border runtime routing: our smart routing layer can direct traffic by policy (region preference, cost tier). When a request is routed from EU edge to US inference nodes, payloads are transmitted over TLS 1.3 and we log the routing decision. There is no automatic replication of request payloads to other regions. Any logs that record routing metadata are stored in the control plane region configured for the customer — for private deployments the control plane can be VPC-local.

I’ll pull our evidence pack (runtime export matrix, sample audit entries, and an extract from the DPA annex wording) and send by EoD. Looping in Kimberly (security controls) to add the link to the audit log sample.

Hi Hannah — a couple of operational clarifications from Security: 

- In-memory only: The serving runtime’s KV cache is ephemeral and scoped to a single inference session in the GPU worker process. We do not serialize the KV cache to disk or to object storage as part of normal operation.
- Optional persistence: For customers who opt into checkpointing for long-running streaming jobs, persistence is explicit, must be enabled in the customer config, and is stored in customer-controlled object storage (S3/GCS) or in a customer VPC when using Private deployments.
- Audit trails: Route decisions and request metadata (request id, source edge, target node id, timestamp) are recorded in the control plane audit log for 90 days by default on Hosted plans; retention can be configured for Dedicated/Private. We can provide redacted sample log lines and a log ingestion sample.

Attaching: redwood-runtime-export-matrix-v1.xlsx (matrix of routing scenarios + controls) and a short DPA excerpt we recommend for the annex.

If you want stricter guarantees, we recommend: pinning region to US-only in the routing policy and enabling a Dedicated or Private deployment so the control plane and compute remain in your tenancy.

Kimberly Park
Security Engineering — Redwood Inference

Hi Marco / Hannah — quick answer to the log schema Q so legal can script checks: our audit log sample includes the following JSON keys (redacted example):

{"request_id": "req_6b2f...", "source_edge_region": "eu-west-1", "target_node_region": "us-east-1", "routing_policy_id": "policy_pin_us_only", "timestamp": "2028-04-23T03:12:08Z", "payload_present": false}

Notes: 
- payload_present is a boolean our control plane sets to indicate whether a request payload was persisted in a downstream artifact; in Hosted defaults this is false.
- We do log hashed identifiers when customers request PII-safe analytics. The actual hashed identifier field is "subject_hash" in the sample.
- For customers that enable edge-level redaction we can show a sample of the redaction transform (hashing/salt) and the resulting audit line.

I’ve attached a redacted log snippet and the recommended Annex B wording in the DPA extract. If you want, we can export a one-off CSV with the sample keys so your legal automation team can validate schema mapping.
